failures.criterion: A1: one command stands the copy up, runs, and tears it down, with the lock that makes an abandoned run reclaimable (plan D5: 'lock ConfigMap with holder, start and 60 s heartbeat, stale after 15 min with the down command named')
failures.evidence: Measured live, not reasoned: run lt-20261029t215258-9b0d's `cluster.sh all` process was killed at 22:16:31Z (its last log line) while this worker pod went on running. At 22:24:01Z `kubectl -n loadtest get configmap dispatch-loadtest-lock` still read heartbeat 2026-10-29T22:23:04Z, 57 s old, and `ps -eo pid,ppid,args` showed only the detached `cluster.sh _heartbeat` (pid 1325, ppid 1) and `_sampler` (pid 1875) of that run, with no `cluster.sh all`, no loadgen, and the whole full-size copy (Dispatch 16 CPU, Postgres 16 CPU, three NATS pods, the 8 CPU runner) still Running. `start_daemon` (cluster.sh:644-646) starts both daemons under setsid, and `cmd__heartbeat` (cluster.sh:687-708) ends only when the lock is gone or names another run, so the heartbeat renews the lock for ever after any death of the run's command that skips the EXIT trap: a SIGKILL, an OOM, or the Legion daemon interrupting the worker's turn, which is how this one died. The lock's age therefore never passes 15 min, `up` never reaches the stale path that names the down command, and its refusal tells the next caller to 'wait for that run to end', which never happens; the copy burns about 46 CPUs until a person finds it. Red test: cluster.test.sh case (o), `the heartbeat stops once no command of its run is alive, so an abandoned run's lock goes stale`, commit ff4dcd85. `cd packages/envoy && bash loadtest/cluster/cluster.test.sh` exits 1 with `FAIL: the heartbeat daemon (pid 2878) still runs 5 s after the last command of its run ended: it renews the lock for ever, so the lock never goes stale and the copy is never reclaimed`, after the 38 earlier cases pass.
